combinations.magnitude: GSK101-induced reduction of paw-withdrawal threshold reversed by GSK219
combinations.evidence_quote: Indeed, a single i.t. injection of GSK101 markedly reduced the paw-withdrawal threshold, which was reversed by coapplied GSK219 (Figure 7A).

combinations.model: i.t. GSK101 in Trpv4 KO mice
combinations.evidence_quote: Moreover, GSK101-induced mechanical allodynia was significantly abolished in global Trpv4 KO mice (Figure 7B) and microglia-specific Trpv4 cKO mice (Figure 7C), but not in endothelial cell-specific or neuron-specific Trpv4 cKO mice (Figure 7D and Supplemental Figure 4I).

combinations.readout: LCN2 mRNA and protein release in cultured spinal microglia
combinations.magnitude: GSK101-induced Lcn2 upregulation and release suppressed by GSK219
combinations.evidence_quote: Consistent with the genetic ablation studies, chemical activation of TRPV4 by GSK101 for 48 hours induced Lcn2 mRNA upregulation in cultured spinal microglia (Figure 9D) and promoted the release of LCN2 protein in cell culture supernates (Figure 9E), which were suppressed by coapplication of GSK219.

combinations.readout: sEPSC frequency/amplitude, AP firing frequency, dendritic spine density
combinations.magnitude: GSK101-induced increases reduced by Lcn2 deficiency
combinations.model: spinal lamina IIo neurons, i.t. GSK101 in Lcn2 KO mice
combinations.evidence_quote: In addition, Lcn2 deficiency effectively reduced the increase in frequency and amplitude of sEPSCs, AP firing frequency (Supplemental Figure 13, K–N), and the density of dendrite spines (Supplemental Figure 13, Q and R) induced by i.t. injection of GSK101 for 3 consecutive days.

combinations.readout: [Ca2+]i transients in spinal Vglut2+ interneurons (in vivo 2-photon)
combinations.magnitude: GSK101-evoked Ca2+ rise abolished by GSK219 pretreatment
combinations.evidence_quote: Using in vivo 2-photon imaging, we found that i.t. injections of GSK101 evoked a rise in [Ca2+]i transients in the spinal Vgult2+ interneurons, which was abolished by GSK219 pretreatment (Figure 7, E–H).
